questions.prompt: The primary motor cortex is located in the

options.text: precentral gyrus of the frontal lobe
postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe
calcarine sulcus of the occipital lobe

questions.explanation: The precentral gyrus (Brodmann area 4) initiates voluntary movement. The postcentral gyrus is the primary somatosensory cortex, which is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: Broca's area, concerned with the production of speech, lies in the

options.text: inferior frontal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere

questions.explanation: Damage causes an expressive aphasia, in which comprehension is relatively preserved. The superior temporal gyrus is the site of Wernicke's area, which handles comprehension.

questions.prompt: A patient speaks fluently but with meaningless words and cannot understand speech. The lesion is most likely in

options.text: Wernicke's area, in the posterior superior temporal gyrus

questions.explanation: Fluent but meaningless speech with poor comprehension suggests receptive aphasia. Broca's lesions give non-fluent speech with relatively good comprehension.

questions.prompt: The primary visual cortex lies around the

options.text: calcarine sulcus in the occipital lobe

questions.explanation: Visual information from the contralateral visual field is received around the calcarine sulcus. The lateral sulcus separates the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes, and the central sulcus separates motor from sensory cortex.

questions.prompt: The fibres of the corticospinal tract cross to the opposite side mainly at the

options.text: anterior commissure of the spinal cord
pyramidal decussation in the lower medulla

questions.explanation: About 85 to 90 percent of the fibres cross at the pyramids. For that reason, a lesion above the decussation causes weakness on the opposite side of the body.

questions.prompt: A patient has a stroke in the left internal capsule. The expected motor deficit is

options.text: weakness of the right side of the body
weakness of the left side of the body

questions.explanation: The internal capsule is above the pyramidal decussation, so the corticospinal fibres have not yet crossed. The left capsule therefore controls the right side.

questions.prompt: The dorsal column-medial lemniscus pathway carries

options.text: fine touch, vibration and conscious proprioception

questions.explanation: These fibres ascend ipsilaterally in the cord and cross in the medulla. Pain and temperature travel in the spinothalamic tract, which is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: The spinothalamic tract carries pain and temperature, and its fibres cross

options.text: within a few segments of entering the spinal cord

questions.explanation: Second-order neurones cross through the anterior white commissure soon after entry. Crossing in the medulla is a feature of the dorsal column pathway.

questions.prompt: Parkinson's disease results mainly from degeneration of dopaminergic neurones in the
questions.explanation: Loss of dopamine in the nigrostriatal pathway disrupts basal ganglia control, causing tremor, rigidity and bradykinesia. The hippocampus handles memory, the cerebellar cortex coordinates movement and the occipital cortex processes vision. None is the site of dopamine loss in Parkinson's disease.

questions.prompt: Which of these is part of the basal ganglia?
questions.explanation: The caudate nucleus, putamen and globus pallidus form the basal ganglia. The pons belongs to the brainstem, which is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: The thalamus acts as a relay station for sensory information to the cortex for all senses EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Olfactory fibres reach the olfactory cortex directly without a thalamic relay. The other senses do relay in specific thalamic nuclei. Vision relays in the lateral geniculate nucleus, hearing in the medial geniculate nucleus and touch in the ventral posterior nuclei.

questions.prompt: A lesion of the right cerebellar hemisphere produces incoordination (ataxia) on the

options.text: right side of the body (same side)

questions.explanation: The cerebellum acts ipsilaterally because of a double crossing of its pathways. The effect on the left side would apply to a cerebral lesion.

questions.prompt: Which cranial nerve supplies the lateral rectus muscle of the eye?
questions.explanation: The rule is LR6 SO4: the lateral rectus is supplied by VI, the superior oblique by IV, and the rest by III. Damage to VI stops the eye from moving outward. The oculomotor nerve supplies most of the other eye muscles, the trochlear nerve supplies the superior oblique, and the trigeminal nerve carries facial sensation and moves the jaw.

questions.prompt: Taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue is carried by the

options.text: facial nerve, through the chorda tympani

questions.explanation: The chorda tympani, a branch of the facial nerve, carries taste from the front of the tongue. The glossopharyngeal nerve serves the posterior third.

questions.prompt: The anterior communicating artery of the circle of Willis connects the

options.text: internal carotid and posterior cerebral arteries

questions.explanation: It joins the anterior cerebral arteries across the midline at the front of the circle. The posterior communicating arteries connect the carotid and posterior systems.

questions.prompt: Occlusion of the middle cerebral artery on the left (dominant) side typically causes

options.text: right-sided weakness affecting the face and arm more than the leg, with aphasia
left-sided weakness with a leg predominance
isolated loss of vision on the left

questions.explanation: The face and arm areas lie on the lateral surface supplied by the middle cerebral artery. The leg area lies medially and is supplied by the anterior cerebral artery. Left-sided weakness would need a lesion on the right, and weakness that favours the leg points to the anterior cerebral artery.

questions.prompt: The cerebral aqueduct connects the
questions.explanation: CSF flows from the lateral ventricles through the interventricular foramina into the third ventricle, then through the aqueduct to the fourth ventricle. Blockage of the aqueduct leads to hydrocephalus.

questions.prompt: The cerebrospinal fluid circulates in the

options.text: subdural space, between dura and arachnoid
space between the skull and scalp
subarachnoid space, between the arachnoid and pia mater

questions.explanation: CSF fills the subarachnoid space and the ventricles. The subdural space is a potential space where bleeding collects after head injury.

questions.prompt: In an adult, the spinal cord ends (conus medullaris) at about the level of
questions.explanation: The cord is shorter than the vertebral column, so lumbar puncture is done below L2 (usually L3 to L4) to avoid the cord. T1 and C7 are far too high, and S2 is where the dural sac ends, not the cord.

questions.prompt: The sympathetic nervous system has its preganglionic cell bodies in the
questions.explanation: The craniosacral outflow (cranial nerves III, VII, IX, X and S2 to S4) belongs to the parasympathetic system.
